lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Imagine an artist in Blender who needs a mesh that lives in a cloud bucket. Do they really have to leave the app, download it, and import it by hand?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's what most of us do. Is there a better way?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Antoine has a fork called bloc that explores exactly that: a Blender panel for browsing assets in AWS S3 and MinIO. It's a fork of an existing add-on by another author, and he keeps that credit.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So how does the panel know which storage to talk to?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Through connections. Each one has a provider, an endpoint, a bucket and a region. Preferences can hold several of them, with one marked active, and the client setup picks the S3 or MinIO path from that choice.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And object storage doesn't really have folders, right?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Right, it has keys. The add-on splits those keys on the slash and builds a nested structure, so the panel can show a hierarchy without pretending it's a local file system.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: There's fuzzy search with RapidFuzz. It scores file names and path pieces, favors direct matches, and filters for scenes, meshes, images and materials.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Okay. And import is just download and done?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Not quite, and this is the detail Antoine stresses. Downloading and importing are two different steps. After the download, a loader picks an importer for STL, OBJ, PLY or USD variants. Anything else gets rejected with a message.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So the listing can work while the import fails.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Exactly. He also notes a limit: the code uses one S3 listing request, so very large buckets would need pagination.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I like that he's upfront about the edges.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Same for scope. The fork was ten commits ahead and five behind upstream when he checked, and that doesn't mean upstream accepted anything. The full write-up has the diagram of the browse and import paths.
